thread.title: Black Friday: How Target, Walmart, Amazon Deals And Shipping Match Up

author: ELAINE LOW
title: Black Friday: How Target, Walmart, Amazon Deals And Shipping Match Up

organizations.name: amazon deals and shipping match up if black

text:
If Black Friday is any indication of the kind of holiday season that retailers are going to have, then it looks like Christmas will be pretty green this year.
X Shoppers have spent $643 million (and counting) online so far as of 10 a.m. ET on Friday, according to Adobe Analytics data, marking 27.8% sales growth from last year. That's on top of the $3.7 billion in online shopping they did on Thanksgiving Day itself, which marked similar year-over-year gains.
And perhaps unsurprisingly, smartphone shopping hit a new peak: Adobe said that Thanksgiving 2018 was the first day of the season to see $1 billion in smartphone sales, three days ahead of last year's first billion-dollar day.
With consumer spending still strong and unemployment low, the competition is looking cutthroat. Here's what each major retailer is offering for the Black Friday weekend and beyond.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Target's Black Friday Target ( TGT ) said late Thursday that its TVs, iPads and Apple ( AAPL ) Watches were selling well, spurred by early Black Friday deals . Gamers gravitated toward the Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One. Lego, L.O.L. Surprise!, Playskool Friends Tickle Me Elmo, Barbie and board games were the toys flying off shelves fastest, as Target looks to pick up on market share left open by the demise of Toys R Us.
Like most major retailers, Target has been aggressive in its bid to win the online customer. This year, the company said it has made more Black Friday products available for online-order pickup and has given sales associates the ability to provide customers with mobile checkout so shoppers can avoid checkout lines. Consumers can also use the Target app to scan its catalog pages and add those products to their digital shopping carts or wish lists.
Adobe said customers' orders to buy online for in-store pick up have shot up 91% on Thursday from the day before.
On Target's earnings call earlier this week, management pointed to the opportunity available in toy sales after having increased the amount of shelf space and inventory for toys in its brick-and-mortar stores.
The shipping and delivery battle is fierce, thanks (or no thanks) to Amazon.com ( AMZN ). Target is offering free two-day shipping with no minimums.
And the promotions don't stop on Black Friday. Target is offering an additional 15% off products on its website on Cyber Monday.
"We're right where we expected to be and we're set up well for a very strong holiday season," said CEO Brian Cornell on the call Tuesday. But Target fell short of expectations in Q3 , sending shares plummeting Monday.
Shares closed down 2.7% on the stock market today .
Walmart's Black Friday The country's largest brick-and-mortar retail chain said that Black Friday is "still the best shopping day of the year , and this year was no exception for Walmart."
Walmart reported steady traffic in stores and boasted deep inventory on top-selling items. Hot products included phones, toys, gaming consoles, cookware and TVs.
Similar to Target, Walmart ramped up its toy selection and rolled out in-store mobile checkout technology that allows customers to skip register lines. It also created app-based store maps.
Online, the company also made Black Friday deals available on its website two hours earlier than it previously had. Now that quick delivery times are expected of retailers, Walmart is also offering free two-day shipping on even more items for orders over $35, no membership fee required, plus the option to return items to its stores.
E-commerce growth at Walmart has been strong, with several quarters of sequential acceleration, and management said on its earnings call last week that the retailer has a better online experience and "more robust" assortment of products this year.
"We feel really good about the position," said Walmart VP of Investor Relations Dan Binder on the call. "And I think we'll come out on the other side being winners."
On Cyber Monday , expect Walmart to offer discounted Nintendo Switch consoles, 58-inch Samsung 4k Ultra HD Smart LED TVs and the Apple iPhone 8 Plus.
Amazon's Black Friday With major deals on toys, gaming consoles, electronics and Amazon devices, the e-commerce giant has no doubt prompted Target, Walmart and others to up their shipping and delivery game, amid an ongoing move toward mobile shopping.
"Mobile shopping continues to skyrocket and see increased conversion," said Adobe Digital Insights Director Taylor Schreiner in a statement. "Retailers understand that shopping and buying on smartphones is now the norm for consumers, and as a result are delivering better experiences and optimization on mobile devices."
Three out of five shoppers plan to make purchases online on Black Friday, according to Adobe data, vs. the 43% who intend to shop at brick-and-mortars.
On Friday, Amazon announced its Cyber Monday deals, which again heavily push its own devices, such as the Echo, Fire TV and Ring doorbell, among other products.
Though revenue guidance for the current quarter came in below views, Amazon management said it is "very bullish" on the holiday quarter, telling analysts on its late-October call that it's in "great shape for the holiday" and will have "great capacity for shipping" to its customers.
